artifact: AI-only language quality screen for the existing 850 synthetic emergency-description drafts

ai_language_quality_findings.assessment_method: Per-row conservative AI screening with transparent lexical cues: apparent readability, whether context is sparse, possible code-switch uncertainty, and explicit wording that might influence a reader?s severity interpretation. Short fragments are flagged as context-limited, not automatically incorrect. Mixed-language candidate tags are copied from the existing lexical heuristic summary only.
ai_language_quality_findings.correction_policy: No suggested rewrite was emitted because these synthetic drafts require fluent human review and the AI-only screen cannot safely establish idiomatic Tagalog, Cebuano/Bisaya, or mixed code-switching. Original text is preserved in every row; reviewers may enter corrections separately.
ai_language_quality_findings.interpretation: Cue flags identify visible lexical wording that could anchor a reader. They are language/wording observations only; no label correctness or severity confirmation is implied.

limitations: This is AI-only screening, not a fluent-human review, translation certification, language-ID verification, or responder approval.
Do not treat naturalness or clarity categories as ground truth; Cebuano/Bisaya, Tagalog, and mixed-language cases particularly require fluent reviewers.
Lexical wording cues are not severity labels and do not confirm whether the existing current_label is correct.
No labels were changed, no training dataset/model was modified, and no training or deployment was performed.
All 850 source rows are synthetic drafts, not observed civilian reports.
